interface.name: fl_shell

description.summary: FreeLFS desktop shell protocol

interface.description: Private protocol between flcomp and the desktop programs (flpanel, flsettings). The panel owns the bottom panel and the start menu; the compositor tells it about windows and the panel tells the compositor what to do with them. Several clients may bind fl_shell; every event goes to every binding. Only one client at a time can own the panel.

entry.name: role
entry.summary: the surface already has another role

entry.name: locked
entry.summary: the screen is locked by another client already

request.name: set_panel

description.summary: make a surface the bottom panel

request.description: The compositor places the surface at the bottom edge of the output, left aligned, always above ordinary windows, and keeps the given height free when it maximizes windows. The surface should be as wide as the output (see wl_output.mode). It gets pointer input but never keyboard focus.

request.name: set_menu

description.summary: make a surface the start menu popup

request.description: The surface is shown while it has a buffer attached, directly above the left edge of the panel. While it is shown it has keyboard focus. A click anywhere except on the menu or the panel hides it and sends menu_dismissed; it appears again at the next commit that attaches a buffer.

description.summary: restore (if minimized), raise and focus a window

request.name: set_keyboard_layout

description.summary: switch the keyboard layout

request.description: name is an xkb layout name ("de", "us") or "layout:variant" ("us:intl"). Not saved to disk. Answered by keyboard_layout.

request.name: logout

description.summary: end the session

request.description: flcomp exits with status 0 (the login shell then exits).

event.name: window_added

description.summary: a window was mapped

event.description: Always followed by one window_changed with the full state.

description.summary: the Super key was tapped: open or close the menu
current layout; sent on bind and after every change

request.name: set_flyout

description.summary: make a surface the tray flyout (volume slider)

request.description: Like set_menu, but the surface is shown directly above the panel, horizontally centred on x (output pixels) and kept inside the output. While shown it has keyboard focus. A click anywhere except on the flyout or the panel hides it and sends flyout_dismissed; it appears again at the next commit that attaches a buffer. Sending the request again with the same surface only moves it.

event.name: volume_key

description.summary: a volume key was pressed (or is repeating)

event.description: The compositor swallows XF86AudioRaiseVolume, XF86AudioLowerVolume and XF86AudioMute and tells every binding of version 2 or later: action 0 raise, 1 lower, 2 mute. Held raise and lower repeat.

request.name: set_output

description.summary: try a display mode and scale

request.description: Settings' Display page. width and height 0 keep the current mode; refresh is in Hz; scale is a percentage from 100 to 200 (the desktop is drawn at 100/scale of the mode's size and enlarged for the screen). The compositor applies it at once and answers with output_state whose pending is 15: unless confirm_output arrives within 15 seconds (or the client goes away) the previous mode and scale come back. A refused mode or scale leaves everything as it was and sends output_failed. The setting is not saved; Settings writes mode= and scale= to desktop.conf after confirm_output.

description.summary: keep the mode and scale that set_output applied
go back to the mode and scale from before set_output

request.name: show_osd

description.summary: show the on-screen indicator

request.description: The compositor draws one small indicator (icon and bar) above the panel, centred, for about a second and a half, then fades it out; a new call replaces it. The panel sends it after it handled a volume key, so that volume and brightness (which the compositor handles itself) share one look. kind: 0 volume, 1 brightness, 2 microphone. percent 0-100. flags: 1 muted.

event.name: output_mode

description.summary: a mode of the display

event.description: Sent for every mode the display offers, on bind and after every change, always followed by one output_state. flags: 1 the mode in use, 2 the display's preferred mode.

description.summary: scale and size now, and whether a change waits for confirmation

arg.name: width
arg.summary: the desktop's size in logical pixels

arg.name: pending
arg.summary: seconds left to confirm, 0: nothing waits

description.summary: set_output was refused; nothing changed

request.name: set_notifications

description.summary: make a surface the notification cards

request.description: The surface is shown at the top right of the output, 16 pixels from the right and top edges, above windows, the panel, the menu and the flyout (but not above the lock screen). It gets pointer input only where its pixels are not fully transparent, so the gaps between cards click through to whatever is below; it never has keyboard focus. The client sizes it to the stack of cards and resizes it as cards come and go; attaching no buffer hides it.

request.name: lock

description.summary: lock the screen and show this surface

request.description: The compositor enters the locked state at once: nothing but the given surface (placed at 0,0, meant to cover the output) is shown, it is the only surface that gets pointer or keyboard input, and shortcuts do nothing except the virtual terminal switches (Ctrl-Alt-F1 to F12) and the media keys. Until the surface has a buffer the screen is a solid colour. The lock stays when the client dies: the compositor then starts the lock program again ($FLCOMP_LOCK, default fllock) and, if that does not help, shows a solid colour with a hint to press Enter to restart it. A client that sends lock while another client holds the lock gets the locked error. Every binding of version 4 gets lock_state.

request.name: unlock

description.summary: unlock the screen

request.description: Only the client that sent lock (and whose surface is still the lock surface) can unlock; from anyone else the request is ignored.

event.name: lock_state

description.summary: the screen was locked or unlocked

event.description: Sent to every binding of version 4 when the state changes, and on bind while it is locked. 1 locked, 0 unlocked.

request.name: set_workspace

description.summary: switch to a workspace

request.description: index counts the grid row by row, from 0 (top left) to cols * rows - 1. Out of range is ignored. Answered by workspaces.

request.name: move_window

description.summary: send a window to a workspace

request.description: The window (and the dialogs that belong to it) leaves the current view when it goes to another workspace. The screen stays where it is. Answered by window_workspace.

description.summary: show or hide the workspace overview (Super+Tab)

event.name: workspaces

description.summary: the workspace grid and the one in view

event.description: Sent on bind and whenever the grid (desktop.conf workspaces=COLSxROWS) or the current workspace changes. The grid is cols wide and rows high; workspace numbers run row by row from 0.

event.name: window_workspace

description.summary: the workspace a window is on

event.description: Sent after window_added (and its window_changed) and whenever the window moves.

request.name: set_desktop

description.summary: give a surface the desktop icon layer

request.description: The surface is drawn above the wallpaper and below every window, with its top left corner at x, y (pixels on the output). It is meant to be small: the client sizes it to its icons. Only what is not transparent takes the pointer; everything else falls through, and a window on top of it hides it. It is shown on every workspace. Attaching no buffer hides it. One client at a time; a second request replaces the first surface.

request.name: set_window_entry

description.summary: where the panel shows a window

request.description: The rectangle of the window's entry in the panel surface (surface coordinates, the panel's top left is 0, 0). The compositor shrinks a minimised window towards it and grows a restored one from it. It is only a hint for animations: without it (or with animations off) the window just appears and disappears. Send it again when the entry moves; w = 0 forgets it.

request.name: maximize

description.summary: maximize or restore a window

request.description: Toggles a window between maximized and its old size (a snapped window is maximized). The panel's window menu uses it.

event.name: output_info

description.summary: one display output (monitor connector)

event.description: Sent for every connector on bind and after every change, each followed by its output_mode_info events, and at the end of the list one output_state (the primary output's scale and logical size, pending 0). flags: 1 connected, 2 enabled (lit), 4 primary. width, height and refresh (Hz) are the output's current mode in pixels (the last one used while it is disabled, 0 if it never had one); scale is a percentage (100..200); x and y are its place on the desktop in logical pixels (mode size divided by scale), the top left of the leftmost output is not necessarily 0,0.

event.name: output_mode_info

description.summary: a mode of the output sent just before

event.description: Preferred mode first. flags: 1 the mode in use, 2 the display's preferred mode.

request.name: output_configure

description.summary: change one output; saved in desktop.conf as output.NAME=

request.description: Only for fldisplay (and Settings through it); other clients are ignored like for set_output. flags say which of the values count: 1 mode (width, height, refresh), 2 scale (percent, 100..200), 4 position (x, y), 8 enabled (the value of "enabled"), 16 primary (this output becomes the primary one; "primary" must be 1). The change is applied at once; it is saved in desktop.conf right away and the previous state of all outputs is remembered once for output_revert. There is no automatic revert (the caller asks the person "keep these settings?" and calls output_revert). A refused change (unknown or disconnected output, mode the display does not have, scale giving a desktop below 640x400, the last enabled output switched off) sends output_failed and changes nothing. Every binding of version 9 gets the new output_info list.

request.name: output_revert

description.summary: go back to the outputs as they were before the last output_configure

request.description: Restores mode, scale, position, enabled and primary of every output and saves them. Without a remembered state it does nothing and sends output_failed.
